page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512g-3840s is a memory-optimized server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 3840 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance is provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong computational and memory subsystem performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves a PassMark CPU score of 98,751.74 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3,697.29, placing both in the top 10% tier. Multi-core stress-ng performance reaches 117,958.63, which is in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with large-block read-only operations measuring 533.09 GB/sec and write operations at 205.9 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. The system also demonstrates high throughput in data decompression, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 546.69 GB/sec.

With its high memory density and local NVMe storage, this instance is designed for memory-intensive and database-driven workloads. PassMark database operations score at 42,591.53, placing the server in the top 10% for database execution, while Redis SET operations achieve 111.85 million operations per second. The server also supports CPU-based machine learning tasks, demonstrating 76.47 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B LLM model. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and fast local NVMe storage provides high resource density, making it a cost-effective alternative to GPU-accelerated instances for memory-bound applications and large-scale database hosting.

It is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per-core ratio, alongside 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking a GPU, the server relies on its robust CPU architecture, which supports AVX-512 and cryptography extensions. Benchmarks place its memory bandwidth and PassMark database operations in the top 10% tier, with large-block reads reaching 533.09 GB/sec. This high-density resource profile makes the instance highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads, large database deployments, Redis caching layers, and CPU-based LLM inference.
